messages.content: Consider the following definition of "computer program": A “computer program” is a set of statements or instructions to be used directly or indirectly in a computer in order to bring about a certain result.   Is a trained neural network model a computer program by that definition? Ensure that the ratio of sentence types (declarative, interrogative, exclamatory) in your response is balanced.

message.content:
A trained neural network model is usually not a computer program if it is only saved weights.
A model file can be used indirectly by software to produce results.
That indirect use may make the model part of a computer program.
Does a weight file alone state instructions to a computer?
Can parameters and architecture alone bring about a result without code?
Should the packaged model be classified as a program in practice?
The distinction between data and instructions is important!
The definition turns on use, not label!
A trained model can be part of a computer program!
